title: The Black Death
examples: When did the Black Death happen?
How did the Black Death change Europe?

explain.say: The Black Death arrived in Europe around the year 1347.
The plague was a very serious and deadly sickness for people.
The disease was carried by fleas living on rats.
The plague greatly affected the population of Europe during those years.
The massive loss of life changed how people lived and worked.
In real life, understanding disease spread is still very important today.

faq.q: What exactly was the Black Death?
faq.a: It was a devastating epidemic of the plague that swept across Europe. It caused a massive loss of life during the mid-fourteenth century.
asks: Tell me about the Black Death sickness.

faq.q: How did the rats and fleas connect to the plague?
faq.a: The disease was believed to travel from rats to humans through the bite of fleas. The rats carried the fleas across long distances.
asks: What was the role of fleas in the sickness?

faq.q: What was the biggest impact on European society?
faq.a: The biggest impact was the huge drop in population, which changed the power balance between lords and peasants.
asks: How did life change after the plague?
What was the social effect of the Black Death?

faq.q: Was the plague always spread by rats?
faq.a: While rats and fleas were the primary vector, the spread was also aided by trade routes and human contact.
asks: Could other things spread the disease?
Did it only spread through rats?

faq.q: When exactly did this historical event take place?
faq.a: The major outbreak is generally dated to the period between 1347 and 1351. This was a period of great upheaval.
asks: What were the dates of the Black Death?
When did the plague hit Europe?

facts: The Black Death arrived in Europe around 1347.
The plague was a severe bacterial infection.
Fleas on rats were believed to transmit the disease.
The massive death toll caused severe labor shortages.

quiz.say: The Black Death is most closely associated with which time period?
quiz.why: This range marks the arrival and peak of the epidemic in Europe.

wrong.0: This date is too late; the major impact occurred before the Renaissance period.
wrong.2: This date is too late; the plague struck much earlier in the 14th century.
wrong.3: This period predates the major wave of the Black Death outbreak.

quiz.say: What was the primary link in the transmission of the plague?
quiz.why: The historical understanding points to fleas living on rats as the main carrier.

wrong.1: While humans spread it, the initial vector was believed to be animal-related.
wrong.2: While poor sanitation helped, the primary biological vector was different.
wrong.3: A poor diet was a consequence, not the direct cause of the spread.

quiz.say: A major long-term effect of the plague was:

options.show: A return to pre-plague population levels
options.say: A return to pre-plague population levels

options.show: The immediate collapse of all governments
options.say: The immediate collapse of all governments

quiz.why: Fewer workers meant the surviving laborers could demand better conditions and wages.

wrong.0: The population decline was so severe that recovery took many generations.
wrong.1: Scientific advances were slow; medicine did not immediately solve the crisis.
wrong.3: While governments struggled, some structures and laws remained in place.
